## 2026-09-20 — responsive, explicit private-journal editing

- Continued D04/I03/X01 using game-development, layout-audit, high-resolution,
  input and frontend-checklist skills. Checklist MCP unavailable; used local
  source review, built-browser geometry, interaction tests and screenshots.
- Replaced the independently positioned textarea and tiny canvas editor labels
  with a single native modal dialog. Preserved dark ink/violet/gold styling,
  240-character sanitation, private local/backups-only notes and all existing
  journal/search/controller semantics. Body text is 18px, help/count 16px,
  title 28px, card name 20px; explicit Save note/Cancel actions are at least
  48 physical pixels tall and stay visible when content needs scrolling.
- Dialog positions within the visible canvas/visual viewport intersection.
  ResizeObserver plus window/visual viewport resize/scroll listeners maintain
  alignment. The editor lives outside the landscape gate's hidden/inert stage
  so an unfinished note stays recoverable when the visible height shrinks.
- Removed blur auto-save. Clicking outside, moving focus or resizing neither
  saves nor discards a draft. Save failure keeps the editor and draft open,
  displays/announces a retry/cancel message and preserves the previous note.
  Successful save and explicit cancel clean up the native dialog, observer,
  listeners and pending focus frame; scene shutdown cancels without saving.
- Tab/Shift+Tab cycle within the three editing controls. Native dialog semantics,
  labels, descriptions, focus outlines and error alert support browser access.
  Composition events do not commit/cancel notes. Deferred initial focus prevents
  the opening J keystroke from entering the note. Codex Confirm/Back reject
  key repeats so held Enter cannot save and then close the underlying card.
- The editor freezes pending reader movement and owns wheel input. Closing
  preserves the same card and scroll position. Controller A/B retain their
  existing save/cancel semantics. This is automated browser coverage, not a
  claim of completed physical-controller, IME or assistive-device certification.

Current follow-up: Same-seed route reward fidelity from the comprehensive product audit. The title and outcome surfaces promised replayable/shareable route seeds, but several player-visible route rolls still consumed ambient `Math.random()`, so identical runs could diverge after audio or cosmetic FX activity and after a save/resume. Route Cache outcomes, two-card drafts, single-card grants, Waymark grants, Supply grants, and nested random route effects now derive from one stable seed/state/salt contract covering the flight seed, district, current node, decision key, deck/Preen state, held Waymarks and Supplies, Cohesion, and Scrap. Reopening a decision keeps its frozen projection, resuming the same state reproduces it, and different seeds retain reward variety; record IDs and cosmetic particle/audio jitter intentionally remain outside the gameplay contract. Focused Chromium coverage proves replay/resume equality under three hostile ambient-randomness values, broad cross-seed variety, structured route-draft quality, and exact preview-to-commit parity across route event families. Strict TypeScript, production build, docs, runtime data, 961 runtime assets, world/FX contracts, deployment cache, enemy-variety/card-overlay contracts, 32 content checks, encounter balance, and the 500-seed economy audit pass; the consolidated gate finishes with all 55 interaction-heavy sequencing scenarios green in 16.5 minutes. The app entry is 675.3 KiB and combined boot is 705.3 KiB, below their hard budgets; the ~0.3 KiB aspirational entry warning is retained because moving this shared contract into the already-tight game-core chunk correctly fails its harder 30 KiB boundary. The required shared production client reached a fully interactive/full-art Rooftop Blocks route in 1.35 seconds with no pending, failed, or timed-out asset groups and no browser-error artifact; the inspected capture is `.artifacts/visual-audit/seeded-route-rewards-shared-client/shot-0.png`. Temporary choreography was deleted, preview port 43160 was stopped, and final cleanup confirms ports 43160 and 5373 are free, unreachable, and have no matching workspace Node/browser processes.

Current follow-up: Contextual route gains from the comprehensive product audit. Reachable nodes already named a category-level gain and their authored pressure, but the route still could not answer `why this path now?` from the current flight. A shared decision policy now keeps the existing two-row `GAIN / RISK` hierarchy while making gain copy live: combat drafts name deck size; Basins show effective healing after the Cohesion cap; Nests count only meaningful Preen targets and show held Scrap; Markets show purchasing Scrap plus deck size; Caches show open Supply capacity; and Signals show available versus total authored choices after current costs and requirements. Boss reward/test authority remains district-authored, encounter risks retain their two-pressure cap, and no future random reward is exposed. The same exact read flows through the top decision dock, hover dossier, serialized route node, and opt-in screen-reader narration without adding persistent map clutter. ## 2026-07-28 Persistent Metadata-Aware Codex Card Search

- Added a dedicated Codex `FIND CARDS` field that composes with the active card
  set, Favorites/Hunt List views, and Collection Lens. Multi-token,
  case/diacritic-insensitive matching covers the card metadata the game
  actually models: name, rules/effects, keywords, bird/character, set/suit,
  kind/type/target, cost, rarity, and ownership.
- Search deliberately protects discovery. Discovered cards expose their useful
  searchable dossier metadata; unfound cards match only safe structural/family
  and ownership terms, so a hidden card cannot be revealed by searching its
  name or rules. The zero-result panel names the query and gives a direct edit/
  clear path instead of leaving an empty binder.
- Pointer/touch opens a real native search input; `/`, focused Confirm, and
  controller `RB` use the same path. Enter applies, Escape restores the
  pre-edit query, Tab/focus-ring navigation includes the control, and the field
  has a 40-character limit plus a full screen-reader label. The editor keeps a
  physical 190x46 minimum target at the 1000x560 supported floor and dismisses
  itself whenever the authoritative platform gate hides the game.
- The query persists in `birdsquad.codexCardSearch`, appears in
  `render_game_to_text`, is announced with result/lens counts, and is included
  in local Flock Record export and transactional restore. Legacy backups safely
  default to an empty query.
- Strict TypeScript passes. The six neighboring Codex focus/favorite/Hunt/
  Lens/search scenarios pass together, and the focused search plus backup/
  restore run passes 3/3. Full `npm run validate` passes all validators and all
  24 critical sequencing scenarios. Production remains at 676.9 KB / 179.4 KB
  gzip app entry, 706.9 KB / 190.3 KB gzip combined boot, and 30.0 KB game
  core; the lazy Codex scene is 89.5 KB / 23.2 KB gzip. The unchanged 1.9 KB
  app-entry preference advisory remains while every hard budget passes.
- Inspected captures:

  `.artifacts/test-results/codex-card-search-minimum-landscape-editing.png`.

## 2026-07-28 Persistent Privacy-Safe Codex Card Sorting

- Split the existing Find Cards header control into two clear, independent
  targets without increasing header density. `SORT` cycles through `Binder`,
  `Name`, `Rarity`, and `Recent`; its current state remains visible beside the
  search query and composes with set tabs, Favorites/Hunt List, Collection
  Lens, and search results.

  visible metadata while unfound slots remain in stable binder order. Recent
  uses the journaled `firstAcquiredAt` provenance for collected cards, then

  acquisition inference is exposed.

  independently from Find. `render_game_to_text` exposes visible, discovered,

The existing normal-motion enemy phase already had long preamble/wind-up/release/impact/recovery beats, but `combatTimingDelay()` collapsed all combat delays to `0` whenever the browser reported `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, making player/enemy damage resolution feel instant on those systems. `src/main.ts` now keeps reduced-motion combat readable by scaling combat delays to 55% with a 260ms minimum instead of removing them entirely, preserving the existing reduced-motion avoidance of high-motion FX while still giving enemy turns tactical beats. `tests/smoke.spec.ts` adds `combat reduced-motion enemy turn still holds damage until impact`, which emulates reduced motion, forces a damaging enemy move, and proves preamble/wind-up/release keep Cohesion unchanged until the impact beat. Current follow-up: Enemy-turn gravity/readability timing pass. Added a new `windup` enemy motion cue so the attacker visibly loads up before lunging, strengthened the impact lunge duration/hold, and wired `enemyAttackWindupFx` to the exact move that will resolve so the enemy shows a threat-charge halo, lane streak, glow, motes, and the move label while flock HP remains unchanged. Bird Squad remains live on port 5199.

Current follow-up: Combat attack animation timing pass. Player card input now routes through an animated play path that spends Wingbeat and removes the card immediately, keeps the board locked with `combatAnimationPending`, and delays card effect resolution until the cast/attack FX has had time to reach the target. Enemy roost input now uses an animated enemy phase that renders the enemy-turn banner, clears enemy cover, queues each living enemy's attack motion, waits through a wind-up, resolves that enemy's move, then gives a short recovery beat before the next attacker. Direct combat helpers remain synchronous by default for existing test/balance harnesses, with optional delayed card resolution and UI-only roost pacing. Battle text state now exposes `combatAnimationPending`, and the focused smoke `combat attacks resolve after their animation wind-up` asserts both sides of the fix: during wind-up the pending flag is true and HP is unchanged; after settlement the pending flag clears and damage lands. Bird Squad remains live on port 5199.

Current follow-up: resolved the game-tightness audit items while preserving the intentionally visible/intuitive route map. Content drift is clean again: `audit:content` now matches shipped Fouled/Supply systems and enemy damage data. Signal Spires and High Roost authored route maps now guarantee at least one Basin/Nest safety stop before the boss, reducing late-map zero-safety paths. Information/scout items were reframed into Route Plan effects: `peekNextNodes(N)` now grants +1 Open Sky Guard and softens the next Open Sky increase by N instead of mostly duplicating visible map information; related Supplies, Waymarks, market labels, summaries, and tests were updated from Intel/Scout/Preview language to Plan language. Boss prep now recommends route stops based on low readiness needs, late market presence/route-plan service availability were strengthened, and the High Roost boss was trimmed from four enemies to three, dropping top boss pressure from 178 HP / 54 max-hit stack to 146 HP / 45 while keeping the final multi-pressure identity. Combat texture was tightened by moving several high-throughput draw/resource/setup cards to 2 cost and turning Plume Street Party into tempo/resonance instead of generic Cover. Verification: `npm run audit:content`, `npm run audit:balance`, `npm run audit:economy`, `npm run validate:runtime`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, focused Playwright smoke tests for route plan/market behavior, `npm run build`, and the required `develop-web-game` client against `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` all passed. Live screenshot inspected at `output/web-game/shot-0.png`.

Current follow-up: continued the engineering maintainability refactor. Shared effect parsing now lives in `src/game/effects/effect-parser.ts`; route-effect execution/conditions now live in `src/game/effects/route-effect-runner.ts`; and card-effect resolution now lives in `src/game/effects/card-effect-runner.ts`. `RouteScene` and `BattleScene` provide narrow adapters for scene-owned state, FX, and callbacks instead of owning the core effect switches directly. The route economy smoke test was also updated to assert the current confirm/claim flow for Basin rewards. Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run audit:content`, `npm run validate:runtime`, `npm run audit:balance`, `npm run audit:economy`, focused route/effect Playwright tests, focused combat/card-effect Playwright tests, `npm run build`, and the required `develop-web-game` client against `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` all passed. Latest live screenshot inspected at `output/web-game/shot-2.png`. Next recommended maintainability slices: add direct unit tests around `route-effect-runner` and `card-effect-runner`, then extract market/reward systems from `RouteScene`.

Current follow-up: reviewed game tightness and system meaning after the ability/effect repairs. Static audits found `npm run audit:balance` and `npm run audit:economy` passing, while `npm run audit:content` still reports drift in two enemy move specs, the `fouled` status registry contract, and the old authored Supply count. Live route/combat inspection on `http://127.0.0.1:5173/` produced screenshots at `.artifacts/test-results/systems-review-route.png` and `.artifacts/test-results/systems-review-battle.png`. Main surfaced improvement areas: late-map route safety/pressure guardrails, overexposed route reward information, low-cost combat hand smoothing, overlapping card effect identity, under-leveraged Supply/Market lanes, and stale map/profile documentation.

Current follow-up: resolved the remaining ability/effect meaning gaps. ## 2026-07-28 Immutable Flight Folio Revision Trail

- Added a Revision Trail to Flight Lab so preserved Folio lineages are visible
  and recoverable in-game. The direct parent is prioritized even when a newer
  sibling revision exists, while every active and archived revision in the
  lineage remains selectable.
- Comparison reports positional card replacements, additions, removals,
  Base/Preened state changes, unchanged cards, leader changes, and run-mode
  changes. Current and selected revision summaries clearly identify archived
  targets and show card art for changed entries; complete machine-readable and
  screen-reader state includes every change.
- Restore is immutable: it copies the selected revision's exact leader, mode,
  source seed, card order, and Base/Preened states into a new active revision.
  The current source and selected target remain byte-for-byte preserved, and
  the new revision records the current Folio as its parent.
- Identical playable revisions cannot create redundant restores. Restores also
  refuse safely when all six active slots are occupied; both refusal paths

## 2026-07-31 Deterministic Boss Phase II

- All four district bosses now have authored, named Phase II patterns:
  Tar-Crowned Crow uses `Chokepoint Lockdown`, Canal Gatekeeper uses
  `Floodgate Pressure`, Beacon-Breaker uses `Beacon Overload`, and Roost Warden
  uses `Final Signal`. Runtime-data validation requires every boss to name its
  second phase and reference at least two valid moves; non-bosses cannot define
  one.
- A surviving boss crosses into Phase II exactly once when damage reduces it
  from above half Cohesion to half or below. The transition resets the intent
  loop to its authored opener and clears enemy Cover plus queued attack force,
  so the new Tell is fair and deterministic. Lethal damage skips the
  transition, and further damage below half cannot retrigger it.

  transition, and the combat log, screen reader, debug state, boss dossier,
